entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The cohort is small and defined by congenital lactic acidosis, not by WWOX or any epileptic encephalopathy: the authors report eight participants, five from one randomized trial and three from an exercise trial.
entries.snippet: We now report outcome measures for 5 participants from the RCT of children with congenital lactic acidosis (10) and 3 subjects involved in the aforementioned exercise trial (12).

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. Three of the eight participants had their drug paused or reduced because of periodic asymptomatic worsening of lower-extremity nerve conduction velocity; the sentence says asymptomatic, so the nerve-conduction change is reported without symptoms in these three.
entries.snippet: because of periodic asymptomatic worsening of lower extremity nerve conduction velocity

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. Symptomatic peripheral neuropathy that ended a randomized trial is attributed to a different, older population: a MELAS trial in older adolescents and adults, which the authors contrast with their paediatric-onset cohort.
entries.snippet: These findings contrast with results of a RCT conducted in older adolescents and adults with mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) that ended prematurely because of symptomatic and electrical evidence of exacerbation or new onset of peripheral neuropathy (11).

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The authors give two modifiers of drug exposure that they say influence safety: metabolism of the drug falls with age, and a gene haplotype changes plasma clearance.
entries.snippet: However, DCA metabolism in humans is inversely proportional to age (21) and GSTZ1 haplotype also influences plasma clearance of the drug (13).

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The authors state that their open-label design cannot separate drug effect from underlying disease as the cause of peripheral neuropathy, which limits attributing the nerve changes either to the drug or to the disease.
entries.snippet: This open label study cannot distinguish unequivocally between the relative impact of DCA exposure vs. underlying disease on the frequency or severity of peripheral neuropathy.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The efficacy endpoint is blood lactate, a systemic biomarker in congenital lactic acidosis; it is not a neuronal bioenergetic measurement and nothing in the paper measures brain energy metabolism.
entries.snippet: DCA maintained normal blood lactate concentrations in all patients of this series, even in the three PDC deficient children who chronically consumed diets relatively liberal in carbohydrates.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. Developmental statements in this open-label series are descriptive and uncontrolled: five of the participants had neurodevelopmental delay, and the paper reports that all but one achieved milestones without a comparison arm.
entries.snippet: Patients 1–5 demonstrated mild to profound neurodevelopmental delay complicated in patient 5 by epilepsy that was treated with carbamazepine and diazepam

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The one participant with epilepsy is reported with epilepsy and contractures persisting unchanged on the drug.
entries.snippet: except for patient 5 (whose epilepsy and contractures persisted unchanged), achieved developmental milestones and improved home functionality
